header.subject: Maths
header.title: Reading Pictographs & Tally Charts
header.goal: Children count a row of pictures and show it as tally marks.

card.bring: textbook pp.279-281 · chalk · cut-outs · books, pencils

moves.yesterday: Yesterday we read The Sky bar graph. How many stars? (6)
moves.do: Say “6 is 4 and ___; 6 is 2 and ___; 4 and 2 make ___”; class answers.
Show p.279: count the Kites row; show the number on fingers.
moves.how: One child says how they counted.
moves.say: “Today we count pictures and make tally marks. Where do you count things at home?”

moves.think: I touch each kite once: 4. Then the boxes are empty, so I stop. For how many more: 6 stars take away 2 planets is 4.
moves.do: Chalk the pictograph (Planets 2, Kites 4, Stars 6); read Kites: 4.
moves.say: “Touch each picture once. Stop at the empty boxes.”

moves.do: Q3b: kites and planets in all? Chalk 4 + 2 = 6; tally 4 Kites.
moves.how: Join means add: count on 2 from 4.
moves.say: “In all means join. Four, five, six!”

moves.do: Window side counts aeroplane boxes, other side bird boxes; add to 10.
moves.how: Chalk a box per vote; class colours. Sana and Ali show it first. Check 5 books.

moves.do: Alone: 1. p.280 Q4 Stars row. 2. Colour the graph. 3. p.281 Q1-3.
moves.how: Tally: 5 stars, 4 squares, 3 circles. Done? Stars − kites = stars − planets?
moves.say: “One box for each. Stop at the first empty box.”

sections.mistake: Counts empty boxes (6 kites), or adds for “how many more”. Ask: “Where does the row of pictures stop?”
sections.stuck: Cover the other rows, touch each picture once, stop at the first empty box.

moves.do: Our Fruit: Mango 3, Apple 5. Count apples; show the tally on fingers.
moves.how: Five say how many marks, and why.
moves.say: “Count the pictures, then show the marks.”

sections.correct: 5 apples; 5 tally marks, one for each picture.
sections.success: I can count a row of pictures and show it as tally marks.
sections.ask: How do you know how many tally marks to draw?
sections.listen: Count the pictures in the row; one mark for each.

moves.do: Finish p.279 Q3 and p.281 Q4-5 at home.
moves.how: Check: 4 kites, 6 stars, 2 planets, 6 in all, 4 more stars.

GRADE 1 · MATHS · Ch.12 Data DetectiveDay 2 · 40 min

Reading Pictographs & Tally Charts

Children count a row of pictures and show it as tally marks.
Bringtextbook pp.279-281 · chalk · cut-outs · books, pencils Wordspictograph · title · tally chart · tally mark · total
PRACTICE · 24 of 40 min
5′ 8′ 12′ 12′ 3′
OpenExplainWe DoYou Do✓
★ Your one thing today · in move

Opening

0–5′Full details ›
1

NUMBER SENSE
Yesterday we read The Sky bar graph. How many stars? (6)Say “6 is 4 and ___; 6 is 2 and ___; 4 and 2 make ___”; class answers. Then “Which is more, 2 or 6?” “Four and two … six!”

2

Show p.279: count the Kites row; show the number on fingers. One child says how they counted. “Today we count pictures and make tally marks. Where do you count things at home?”

Explanation · I Do

5–13′Full details ›
3

Chalk the pictograph (Planets 2, Kites 4, Stars 6); read Kites: 4. Pictures only, not empty boxes. “Touch each picture once. Stop at the empty boxes.”Think aloud: “I touch each kite once: 4. Then the boxes are empty, so I stop. For how many more: 6 stars take away 2 planets is 4.”

We Do

13–25′Full details ›
4

I START, YOU FINISH
Q3b: kites and planets in all? Chalk 4 + 2 = 6; tally 4 Kites. Join means add: count on 2 from 4. “In all means join. Four, five, six!”

5

ONE NEIGHBOUR TURN
Window side counts aeroplane boxes, other side bird boxes; add to 10. Chalk a box per vote; class colours. Sana and Ali show it first. Check 5 books. “Count the coloured boxes with me.”Window side first: “Aeroplane boxes: ___.” → Reply: “Bird boxes: ___. Do we make 10?” · Stop: one clap, eyes on me

You Do · in the book

25–37′Full details ›
6

⏱ 25′ stop explaining
Alone: 1. p.280 Q4 Stars row. 2. Colour the graph. 3. p.281 Q1-3. Tally: 5 stars, 4 squares, 3 circles. Done? Stars − kites = stars − planets? “One box for each. Stop at the first empty box.”If stuck: Cover the other rows, touch each picture once, stop at the first empty box.

Check 5 books · answers

1.6 tally marks (||||, then |); total: six
2.Boxes: stars 5, squares 4, circles 3
3.5 stars, 4 squares, 3 circles
Done?No: 6 − 4 = 2, but 6 − 2 = 4

Likely mistake

Counts empty boxes (6 kites), or adds for “how many more”. Ask: “Where does the row of pictures stop?”

THE BOARD BY THE END · a row of pictures, then tally marks

Check · exit ticket

37–40′Full details ›
7

Our Fruit: Mango 3, Apple 5. Count apples; show the tally on fingers. Five say how many marks, and why. “Count the pictures, then show the marks.”Ask: “How do you know how many tally marks to draw?” → Listen for: Count the pictures in the row; one mark for each.Success: “I can count a row of pictures and show it as tally marks.” 👍 or ✊ firstCorrect: 5 apples; 5 tally marks, one for each picture.

Homework

at homeFull details ›
8

Finish p.279 Q3 and p.281 Q4-5 at home. Check: 4 kites, 6 stars, 2 planets, 6 in all, 4 more stars. “Count pictures, not boxes.”
